<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**25** anchor(s) derived from **3** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **23** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ad622d30f6589c7b1f104f55bc3caf1a4d4894dd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `854b8a56144aaa50ae742008249dc1f2b670aa40` — the merge of head `5bd9735277784c115b2a2b4faf3b9a395111644b` into base `ad622d30f6589c7b1f104f55bc3caf1a4d4894dd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 854b8a56144aaa50ae742008249dc1f2b670aa40 && git checkout 854b8a56144aaa50ae742008249dc1f2b670aa40
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ad622d30f6589c7b1f104f55bc3caf1a4d4894dd 5bd9735277784c115b2a2b4faf3b9a395111644b && git checkout -B drift-repro ad622d30f6589c7b1f104f55bc3caf1a4d4894dd && git merge --no-ff 5bd9735277784c115b2a2b4faf3b9a395111644b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ad622d30f6589c7b1f104f55bc3caf1a4d4894dd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line review: #31732, head f28a8b80 · 2026-11-09T06:04Z**

Verdict: **PASS.** Package-less one-row is enforced by the store on every dialect at every moment, every index change is create-before-drop, and no index outside the declared one is dropped.

- **Mongo, `retireWidenedUniques`:**
  - The arm runs only for an unnamed declared `global` unique of 2–8 fields.
  - It requires the wide, driver-built NULL-distinct unique to be present first.
  - It drops only the driver-built proper-subsequence unique by its generated name, never one the schema still wants.
  - When a gained field is nullable, it also requires the exact `{field: null}` partial guard on the narrower key; otherwise the old index stays.
  - On the first upgraded boot, schema sync runs before the `kernel:ready` guard exists, so the old index survives until a later sync sees the guard. There is no window without a constraint.
  - Each retirement is warned, naming the old and new keys.
- **MariaDB:** `INVISIBLE VIRTUAL` `__hash` carrier plus a `UNIQUE KEY`, scoped to `package_id IS NULL` by its stored expression.
  - Measured live on 11.8: it refuses a second package-less row on insert and on update to NULL, it admits two packages once the old key is gone, and it is absent from `SELECT *` and `driver.find`.
  - Naming the carrier as a #11627 hash shadow keeps the orphan-column pass off it.
  - The differ reading it as a partial unique on `(metadata_type, name)` lets driver-sql's widening arm make the one safe replace. The plan comes back empty on the next boot.
  - An unscoped carrier does not count as the guard (pinned).
- **MariaDB before 10.3:** `unsupported`, and it keeps the old index (S1 behaviour). That is the right fail-closed answer.
- The two forced test edits are declared: MariaDB is no longer the "no form" case.

With this landed, #31732's precondition for E children is met: a second package's ledger row is admitted on every dialect that has a guard, and refused where none exists. Seat 4 accepts and lands after green CI. It is not a governed surface.

## ACCEPT · PR #31831 · #31732 · 2026-11-09T06:55Z

Head-sha: `5bd9735277784c115b2a2b4faf3b9a395111644b`

- **Seat review (TIER_DEFAULT; `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`; no contract review is owed, no published schema and no governed path):**
  - **Mongo:** `retireWidenedUniques` runs after the create loop. It retires a narrower unique only when it is driver-built (the NULL-distinct or legacy sparse shape), named by the driver's own `idx_<fields>_unique`, not wanted by any current op, and a proper in-order subsequence of an unnamed declared global unique whose driver-built wide index is confirmed present. A nullable gained field also requires the exact `{field: null}` partial guard on the narrower key; otherwise the old index is kept. One `warn` per retirement, and `IndexNotFound` (27) from a concurrent sync is tolerated. Right.
  - **MariaDB:** the package-less guard is an `INVISIBLE VIRTUAL` carrier, `uniq_sys_metadata_activation_packageless__hash`, with a `UNIQUE KEY`. Its stored expression is `CASE WHEN package_id IS NULL THEN digest END`. `parseHashShadowRowScope` makes introspection read it as a partial unique on `(metadata_type, name)`. It is never an orphan, and it is the guard `hasPartialUniqueGuard` (now read through the enforced key) asks for, so driver-sql's widening arm makes the one safe `replace_unique_index`. A re-boot re-keys after `ER_DUP_FIELDNAME`. MariaDB is told apart from MySQL by `SELECT VERSION()`, and an unreadable answer takes the MySQL form. MariaDB before 10.3 stays `unsupported` and keeps the old index. Right.
  - **New names** (the seat's call): the carrier column follows `hashShadowColumnFor` (index name + `__hash`), which the differ requires. The new exports are module-level only, and no root `index.ts` changed, so `Clause-②: no` holds. Kept.
- **Epic red-line review:** PASS on this head, 6733460765. The package-less one-row stays store-enforced on every dialect at every moment, every change is create-before-drop, and no undeclared index is dropped. This meets the precondition for the E children.
- **Dev's measured conditions (report 6733426622):** the MariaDB live cell shows the carrier absent from `driver.find` and `SELECT *`, a plan of exactly one safe replace with no drops, and an empty re-plan. The Mongo recording Db shows the drop after both creates, and that a nullable gained field with no guard keeps the old key. Ablations C1–C3, C5 and C7 go red.
- **Main merge:** `5bd97352` merges `f28a8b80` (all green: 35 passed, 15 skipped; the epic PASS is on it) with `main` `ad622d30`. It had no conflicts. The net +/- lines against the merge base are byte-identical to `f28a8b80`'s (sha256 `685a8967…`).
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, and patch for driver-mongodb, driver-sql and metadata-protocol, per ruling A on #25105. Claim 6730873579 and the MariaDB scope addendum 6729603260 cover every file in the diff.
- **Gates on this head:** 35 success, 15 skipped, 0 failed or pending on `5bd97352`; NOT governed (0 of 9 paths); K = 2; mergeable_state clean.
- **Landing:** `pr_ready` and `automerge_enable` happen in this stroke. The card closes on merge (`Fixes #31732`).
